title: Pokémon Wildclash
description: Original Kanto Pokémon, cinematic live-action battles, classic commands and realistic elemental attacks.

genesis.worldPrompt: High overhead 35mm camera pitched downward 65 degrees; ground fills the frame. Red is NEAR LOWER-LEFT x25%, y70%, rear three-quarter facing upper-right. Blue is FAR UPPER-RIGHT x76%, y32%, front three-quarter facing lower-left, several body lengths farther away. Full bodies in their quadrants, trainers behind. Exactly one Pokémon per occupied side, at most two total. Hyperreal Kanto anatomy and natural woodland materials. Dramatic, energetic, beautiful attacks with explosive acceleration, brilliant elemental light, one crescendo and weighted recovery. Preserve accepted hit, miss, immunity, HP and winner. No UI, text or subtitles. Speak only the accepted English trainer line once. Send-outs and attacks are urgent FIFO, targeting playback five seconds after selection. Prefer exact ready BEFORE-action cached frames; continue immediately if unavailable. The LLM calls cache_image; the server asynchronously generates and saves it. Announce battle begins after send-out playback completes. Vary light, foliage and gentle idle gestures while preserving visible canon. Group prose: overview/style; each team with appearance, trainer, position and opening state; camera/environment once; action.

animateBattles.description: Show accepted moves in the shared live video stream
animateBattles.label: Animate Battles

rejoinCooldownSeconds.label: Rejoin Cooldown
rejoinCooldownSeconds.description: Cooldown in seconds after fainting before rejoining

turnSeconds.label: Command Timer
turnSeconds.description: Seconds to choose a command. At zero, use the selected available move. Zero disables the timer.

battleCamera.label: Battle framing
battleCamera.description: Elevated downward view keeps both Pokémon inside the lower-left and upper-right quadrants.
battleCamera.default: High overhead 35mm battle camera pitched downward 65 degrees onto the clearing. Ground fills the frame; keep the horizon and sky above the crop. Red is the NEAR foreground Pokémon, LOWER-LEFT at x25%, y70%, rear three-quarter facing upper-right. Blue is the FAR background Pokémon, UPPER-RIGHT at x76%, y32%, front three-quarter facing lower-left. Blue stands several body lengths farther from the lens; perspective makes an equally sized creature smaller there. Show backs, heads and feet from above, with both full bodies inside their quadrants and open diagonal ground between them. Trainers stay behind their own Pokémon. Exactly one Pokémon per occupied side, at most two total. Preserve identities and scale through each shot. At a fresh-frame cut, establish this overhead composition immediately.

videoActionTiming.label: Video action timing
videoActionTiming.description: Action choreography across delayed continuous video chunks.
videoActionTiming.default: Attacks are dramatic, energetic and beautiful: explosive acceleration, powerful windup, one clear elemental crescendo and impactful contact around two seconds, then weighted recovery. Use brilliant fire and embers, branching electricity, translucent water, glittering spray, crystalline frost, volumetric light and wind-driven dust as appropriate to the accepted move. Preserve the recorded hit, miss, immunity, HP and winner. Effects remain light, water, debris or energy; keep one creature body per side. One accepted move per 5.17-second shot. Trainer callout and windup start in the first second, contact around two seconds, then the recorded reaction. A knockout is followed by a separate full shot lingering beside the fainted Pokémon, then a separate full shot for an unhurried Poké Ball recall. Show gentle breathing and the trainer kneeling during the pause. During recall, spend the first two seconds aiming the ball, the middle of the shot drawing the whole Pokémon into soft red light, and the final second closing and holding the ball. Admit the next trainer after recall playback finishes. Idle shots show breathing, wind, foliage and settling dust. All speech is English. Wordless shots state: No words are spoken. Hold the high overhead view and near-left/far-right depth throughout.

visualContext.label: Generate setup frames
visualContext.description: Prepare a library of scene-only lineup and aftermath checkpoints ahead of events, then apply matching frames at safe stream boundaries.

setupImagePrompt.label: Scene start frame prompt
setupImagePrompt.default: High overhead 35mm battle camera pitched downward 65 degrees onto the clearing. Ground fills the frame; keep the horizon and sky above the crop. Red is the NEAR foreground Pokémon, LOWER-LEFT at x25%, y70%, rear three-quarter facing upper-right. Blue is the FAR background Pokémon, UPPER-RIGHT at x76%, y32%, front three-quarter facing lower-left. Blue stands several body lengths farther from the lens; perspective makes an equally sized creature smaller there. Show backs, heads and feet from above, with both full bodies inside their quadrants and open diagonal ground between them. Trainers stay behind their own Pokémon. Exactly one Pokémon per occupied side, at most two total. Preserve identities and scale through each shot. At a fresh-frame cut, establish this overhead composition immediately. Rebuild the reference from above. Hyperrealistic live-action fantasy cinematography. Recognizable first-generation Kanto Pokémon with believable biology, natural proportions, detailed scales, fur, wet skin, weathered shell and wing membranes. Rugged woodland clearing, wet earth, moss, distant mist, warm low sun and cool shadows. Real mass, inertia, contact shadows, physically grounded fire, turbulent water, branching electricity, airborne debris and environmental reactions. Photographic creature effects, cinematic contrast and restrained color. Show only the accepted lineup in settled poses. Match iconic species silhouettes with natural biological materials. Physical scene only, no UI, HUD, health bars, levels, numbers, text, labels, captions, menus, buttons, icons or watermark. Reconstruct clean scenery beneath reference graphics. Internal starting frame only.

imageGenerationPolicy.label: When to generate start frames
imageGenerationPolicy.default: Prepare a fresh ready frame for every round and refresh idle ready frames after 30 seconds. Check every 15 seconds and cut to each newly accepted image at the next safe boundary. Keep actions responsive while images prepare. Each cut restores the steep overhead near-left/far-right composition with exactly one Pokémon per occupied side. Keep fainting forecasts ready. Send-outs and attacks use exact ready BEFORE-action start frames when available, otherwise continue immediately. Send-out images leave the releasing position empty with its trainer holding a closed ball. Attack images show the accepted pre-impact state. Cache preparation never blocks an urgent action. After the fainting hold, recall remains linked and the Pokémon stays inside its ball. Internal start images never appear as still overlays.

actionDrivenVideo.label: Prioritize battle actions
actionDrivenVideo.description: Legacy setting. Continuous idle animation remains enabled by the host.

damageMultiplier.label: Attack damage
damageMultiplier.description: Multiply calculated attack damage to give battles more rounds.

maxHitHpFraction.label: Maximum damage per hit
maxHitHpFraction.description: Cap one attack at this fraction of the target’s full HP, including critical and super-effective hits.
